A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Stable-RAG and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–C. Corresponding material can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original QA benchmark results, ablations, permutation-sensitivity measurements, and hidden-state analyses, including appendix experiments.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results and adds a LLaMA-3.3-70B hidden-state clustering analysis.

M1.justification: Permutation enumeration, spectral clustering, representative decoding, FC/PC/FU/FA preference construction, and DPO alignment remain unchanged. The revised decoding setting in Appendix A.3 does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use NQ, TriviaQA, and HotpotQA with the same retrieval, document-order, transfer, and unanswerability scenarios. The added 70B diagnostic uses the existing NQ/DPR scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators, including Vanilla RAG/SFT, RetRobust, ATM, RAAT, Pos2Distill, Ms-PoE, standard DPO, and exhaustive-decoding Stable-RAG where applicable. Newly cited methods are not added to the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix A.3 changes the reported data-construction decoding from temperature 0.01 to greedy decoding, while retaining inference temperature 0.01. Appendix C.2 extends the existing 1,000-instance NQ/DPR clustering protocol to LLaMA-3.3-70B. The PDFs do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V4 Figure 9 adds a 70B layer-wise clustering diagnostic, extending the analysis of structural instability across model scales. Earlier ablations, sensitivity tests, transfer analyses, and case studies remain; the original-versus-shuffled analysis moves from Appendix C.5 into Section 5.3.

E5.justification: Both versions report fixed seed 42 and retain the same sampling information for existing diagnostics. Neither introduces repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V4 adds cluster-count trajectories for LLaMA-3.3-70B in Figure 9. Existing benchmark scores and plotted results are retained. V1 Table 8 becomes v4 Table 6 with unchanged values, including Stable-RAG's NQ SubEM of 48.14 under original order and 47.23 under shuffled order.

T1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix B retain the same mathematical formulation, similarity matrix, normalized Laplacian, eigengap rule, representative-state selection, and DPO objective. No substantive derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The central claims remain permutation-induced hallucinations, mitigation through clustering and DPO alignment, and improved QA accuracy, consistency, and generalization. Shortened contribution bullets and softened adjectives do not materially change their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix C.2 removes v1's specific assertion that sensitive samples' greater divergence is primarily localized to the middle layers. The broader structural-instability interpretation and limitations concerning intermediate-layer constraints, computational cost, and factual reliability remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 removes the explicit TRL library disclosure and detailed LoRA projection list, retaining 'all projection layers.' V4 also explicitly identifies LLaMA3-8B-Instruct for the positional-robustness experiment. Other principal hyperparameters, hardware information, and code/checkpoint links remain.

R1.justification: V4 substantially expands cited literature across hallucination, retrieval/reranking, abstention, prompting, and model applications, including Set-LLM and numerous recent works in Appendix A.3. Selective-Context and EXIT disappear from the related-work discussion. This broad citation revision retains the central positioning around permutation sensitivity.

P1.justification: V4 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, condenses contribution statements and appendix discussion, and moves the original-versus-shuffled subsection into the main analysis. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V1 Figures 9–10 are combined into v4's eight-panel Figure 9, including the new 70B panel. The shuffled-order table moves from the appendix to the main text, and subsequent tables and figures are renumbered. These are targeted display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The added 70B clustering diagnostic modestly strengthens evidence that the proposed internal-instability explanation extends to larger models, complementing the large-model PSR results already in v1. Moving the shuffled-order comparison into the main analysis improves accessibility. Some implementation disclosures are lost, limiting the net gain; the core method and benchmark conclusions remain unchanged.
